paragraphs.text: He confesses that neither by his own authority, power or policy was his kingdom quiet, but by the secret grace of God.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: To give to God just praise, is to confess ourselves to be unworthy of so excellent benefits, and that he bestows them on us of his free mercy.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: He desires God to continue his graces, and to send help for the present need.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: By these manner of speeches he shows that all the hindrances in the world cannot prevent God's power, which he apprehends by faith.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: That is, deliver me from the tumults of they who should be my people but are corrupt in their judgment and enterprises, as though they were strangers.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: For though they shake hands, they do not keep their promises.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: That is, a rare and excellent song, as your great benefits deserve.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Though wicked kings are called God's servants, as was Cyrus in Isa 45:1, for he uses them to execute his judgments: yet David because of God's promise and they who rule godly are properly so called, because they do not serve their own affections, but set forth God's glory.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: He desires God to continue his benefits toward his people, counting the procreation of children and their good education among the chiefest of God's benefits.
